traditional_storage_methods: Pusa Bin (earthen structure with polyethylene film sandwich layer)
Traditional Morai / Kothi lined with paddy straw and plastered with clay/cow-dung
Layering with dried neem leaves (Azadirachta indica) at 2% w/w ratio to deter rice weevil (Sitophilus oryzae)
Solar sun-drying of grain on clean tarpaulins for 2-3 sunny days prior to bagging
ventilation_guidance: Provide cross-ventilation during dry sunny afternoons (ambient RH < 65%). Close ventilators tightly during night hours, rain spells, or humid mornings to prevent moisture re-absorption.
pest_prevention_guidance: Inspect weekly for Rice Weevil (Sitophilus oryzae) and Lesser Grain Borer (Rhyzopertha dominica). Use hermetic GrainPro bags or earthen kothis sealed airtight. Place neem seed kernel powder packets at bag corners.
spoilage_warning_signs: Musty or fermented sour odor indicating fungal respiration
Grain clumping, caking, or damp crusting on upper bag layers
Localized temperature rise ('hot spots' > 32°C inside grain mass)
Presence of insect frass, webbing, or powdery flour
recommended_actions: If grain moisture exceeds 14%, immediately unload and sun-dry in thin layers (3-5 cm)
If grain temperature spikes above 30°C, aerate and rotate bags to break localized hotspots
Seal storage hermetically if pest emergence is detected in early stages
source_name: ICAR - Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR) & IGGMRI Storage Protocols
applicability_notes: Applies to raw dry paddy stored in gunny bags, HDPE woven bags, or hermetic bins. Parboiled paddy requires strict moisture < 12.5%.

storage_type: Metallic Silo / Covered Warehouse / Earthen Kothi
traditional_storage_methods: Storage in galvanized corrugated steel bins (PAU/IGGMRI bins) kept on raised wooden dunnage
Traditional Buhari / Kothi treated with wood ash and dry camphor at bottom
Admixture of dried wild mint or neem leaves
Surface layering with clean dry river sand (3-5 cm) to suppress insect movement
ventilation_guidance: Keep warehouse sealed during monsoon months. Aerate only when ambient temperature and humidity are lower than inside storage (differential aeration).
pest_prevention_guidance: Primary risks: Khapra beetle (Trogoderma granarium), Rust-red flour beetle (Tribolium castaneum). Keep godown floor disinfected and bags stacked at least 50 cm away from perimeter walls.
spoilage_warning_signs: Hollowed-out grains with visible emergence holes
Floury dust accumulation underneath bag stacks
Rise in temperature inside center of bag piles above 30°C
Sour rancid odor
recommended_actions: Perform solarization by spreading grain under full sunlight on clear tarpaulins for 6 hours
Segregate infested bags from clean stacks immediately
Ensure bottom dunnage is dry and free of dampness
source_name: ICAR - Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research (IIWBR)
applicability_notes: Mandatory that grain moisture is brought below 12% before bulk bagging; higher moisture triggers rapid mould development and heating.

traditional_storage_methods: Traditional elevated bamboo cribs with slatted floors for natural air drying of cobs
Hanging cobs under veranda eaves above cooking hearth where smoke repels weevils
Grain storage in airtight drums with tight rubber gaskets
ventilation_guidance: Continuous natural air flow required while drying on cob. Once shelled, store dry grain in sealed bags with intermittent aeration only during low RH hours.
pest_prevention_guidance: Guard against Maize Weevil (Sitophilus zeamais) and Angoumois Grain Moth (Sitotroga cerealella). Hermetic storage bags drastically reduce oxygen to suppress insects.
spoilage_warning_signs: Greenish-yellow mould dusting (Aspergillus flavus - Aflatoxin indicator)
Clumping of grains and dampness
Noticeable ammonia or stale alcohol odor
recommended_actions: Discard any visibly mould-damaged or discolored grains; never feed mouldy maize to animals
Immediate re-drying if grain moisture approaches 13.5%
Store on raised pallets with rodent barriers
source_name: ICAR - Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR) & FAO Post-Harvest Protocols
applicability_notes: Aflatoxin risk is extremely high in warm, humid climates. Moisture control is critical.

region: Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka
traditional_storage_methods: Storing in intact pods rather than shelled kernels (pod shell provides natural barrier)
Traditional bamboo baskets lined with dried straw and cow-dung wash
Stacking gunny bags on wooden crates 30 cm above ground
Thorough sun-drying pods until pods rattle freely when shaken
ventilation_guidance: Well-ventilated ambient room. Air stagnation combined with humidity causes immediate Aspergillus flavus sporulation producing carcinogenic aflatoxins.
pest_prevention_guidance: Key pest: Groundnut Bruchid (Caryedon serratus) and Red Flour Beetle. Keep storage free from cracked or mechanically injured pods. Clean surroundings thoroughly.
spoilage_warning_signs: Yellowish-green powdery mold inside split shells
Rancid bitter oil taste or pungent smell
Discoloration of seed coat from pinkish to dark brown/black
recommended_actions: Ensure pods are dried to < 8% moisture before storing; shake pods to verify rattling sound
Isolate stacks that show any moisture condensation or mold smell
Do not store near moisture sources or open drains
source_name: ICAR - Directorate of Groundnut Research (DGR), Junagadh
applicability_notes: Always store as dry pods rather than kernels. Kernels lose viability and turn rancid 3x faster.

storage_type: Hermetic Bin / Metal Bin / Lined Gunny Bags
traditional_storage_methods: Smearing seeds with edible oil (mustard, castor, or neem oil at 5ml/kg seed) to prevent pulse beetle egg hatching
Layering with dry sieved river sand (2-3 cm layer on top of bin)
Mixing with wood ash (at 1:50 ratio) in earthen pots
Storage in airtight earthen pots (Matkas) with mouths sealed using cloth and wet clay
ventilation_guidance: Keep storage airtight if using hermetic methods. If in warehouse, keep humidity strictly below 60% and avoid damp air entry.
pest_prevention_guidance: The Pulse Beetle (Callosobruchus chinensis) is devastating. One beetle can cause 80% loss in 3 months. Complete exclusion via hermetic seals or edible vegetable oil coating is highly effective.
spoilage_warning_signs: Circular exit holes ('windows') on grains with white eggs attached to seed coat
White powdery residue accumulating at container bottom
Foul sweetish-stale smell
Grain heating up in localized spots
recommended_actions: Solarize infested seeds on hot days for 4-6 hours to kill all life stages of Callosobruchus
Coat uninfested seed grain with edible vegetable oil (3-5 ml per kg) before bagging
Seal container airtight; pulse beetles suffocate in low-oxygen environments
source_name: ICAR - Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR), Kanpur
applicability_notes: Moisture above 10% drastically escalates pulse beetle multiplication and loss of germination vigor.

traditional_storage_methods: Treatment with castor oil (Ricinus communis) at 5ml/kg seed
Admixture of powdered sweet flag rhizome (Acorus calamus) at 10g/kg
Hermetic sealing in thick polythene-lined mud kothi
Sun-drying for 3 consecutive days to reduce grain moisture below 10%
ventilation_guidance: Store in dry room away from ground dampness. Avoid air exchange during monsoon to prevent moisture uptake.
pest_prevention_guidance: High susceptibility to Callosobruchus maculatus. Pre-storage hygiene is vital. Disinfect old gunny bags with boiling water or solar heating.
spoilage_warning_signs: White insect eggs visible on grain surfaces
Hollow seed coats and weight loss
Presence of insect frass and dust
recommended_actions: Spread seeds in single layer on sunny clear afternoon to kill pulse beetle larvae
Transfer to airtight drums or hermetic bags with minimal headspace
source_name: ICAR - Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR) & ICRISAT
applicability_notes: Applies to whole pulse grain intended for seed or human consumption before splitting into dal.

traditional_storage_methods: Mustard oil coating (5ml/kg) to form a protective lipid film
Mixing with dry red chilli powder or turmeric rhizome pieces
Storage in tin cans with hermetic lids
Sun-drying on clean polythene sheet
ventilation_guidance: Hermetically sealed storage is preferred over ventilated open storage due to high bruchid vulnerability.
pest_prevention_guidance: Green gram is the most vulnerable pulse to Callosobruchus chinensis. Even 2-3 beetles can ruin an entire sack within 6 weeks.
spoilage_warning_signs: Loss of green luster and dulling of seed coat
Pin-sized holes on grains
Clumping due to insect webs
recommended_actions: Solarize immediately if any beetle activity is observed
Store exclusively in airtight containers with oxygen absorbers or dry neem leaf cushion
source_name: ICAR - Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR)
applicability_notes: Dry to 9% moisture or below. Never store freshly harvested damp moong.

traditional_storage_methods: Coating with refined castor or gingelly (sesame) oil (4ml/kg)
Layering with dry wood ash in earthen pots
Thorough drying in direct sun before bin storage
ventilation_guidance: Keep in cool, dry storeroom. Close all openings during humid rainy season.
pest_prevention_guidance: Bruchild beetle prevention is paramount. Inspect fortnightly.
spoilage_warning_signs: Discoloration of black seed coat to greyish tint
Insect emergence holes and powder dust
Moisture absorption feeling soft to touch
recommended_actions: Sun dry for 1-2 days if moisture increases above 10%
Store in sealed plastic drums with tight clamp rings
source_name: ICAR - Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR)
applicability_notes: Requires low ambient humidity to maintain cookability and hardness.

storage_type: Ventilated Warehouse / Gunny Bags on Pallets
traditional_storage_methods: Stacking gunny bags on wooden dunnage with at least 60 cm alleyways between stacks
Limiting stack height to no more than 8 bags to prevent seed compression injury and internal heating
Gentle natural shade drying to preserve delicate seed coat integrity
ventilation_guidance: Provide continuous gentle cross-ventilation during dry weather. Avoid direct hot dry wind that shatters the fragile seed coat.
pest_prevention_guidance: Main damage occurs through mould and Free Fatty Acid (FFA) development rather than weevils. Guard against moisture and high temperatures.
spoilage_warning_signs: Seed coat cracking or wrinkled cotyledons
Loss of natural cream-yellow seed coat luster, turning brownish
Rancid odor indicative of lipid oxidation
Rapid drop in germination rate below 70%
recommended_actions: Do not drop or throw bags as seed embryo is easily damaged
Keep storage temperature below 22°C to prevent oil rancidity
Never store soybean with moisture > 11%
source_name: ICAR - Indian Institute of Soybean Research (IISR), Indore
applicability_notes: Soybean has high lipid (20%) and protein (40%) content; quality degrades rapidly under high humidity.

storage_type: Dry Metal Silo / Traditional Earthen Kothi
traditional_storage_methods: Traditional underground pits (Khatti / Bandha) lined with millet straw and husk
Earthen pots sealed with clay and dry cow dung plaster
Admixture of neem and wild tulsi leaves
ventilation_guidance: Keep dry and airtight. High lipid enzymatic activity causes bitterness if exposed to damp air.
pest_prevention_guidance: Rice weevil and red flour beetle. Keep storage clean and dry.
spoilage_warning_signs: Bitter pungent taste indicating lipase enzyme activation
Grain darkening
Mouldy musty odor
recommended_actions: Sun dry thoroughly before storage
Store whole grain; do not grind flour until immediate consumption
source_name: ICAR - Indian Institute of Millets Research (IIMR), Hyderabad
applicability_notes: Millets possess high natural durability when kept under 11% moisture.

region: Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha
storage_type: Earthen Bin / Metal Bin / Hermetic Container

additional_parameters.exceptional_shelf_life_notes: Ragi has natural seed hardness and polyphenols conferring high natural insect resistance

traditional_storage_methods: Traditional Kanaja / Pathaya (bamboo structure plastered with mud and cow dung)
Underground granaries lined with straw (Hagevu system in Karnataka)
Layering with dry vitex (nirgundi) or neem leaves
ventilation_guidance: Store in sealed dry bins. Very resistant to pests if moisture is maintained below 11%.
pest_prevention_guidance: Rarely attacked by weevils due to small grain size and seed coat hardness. Guard against moisture and rodents.
spoilage_warning_signs: Clumping or crusting due to moisture ingress
Damp earth smell
recommended_actions: Periodic inspection of container seals
Sun dry once a year before monsoon season
source_name: ICAR - Indian Institute of Millets Research (IIMR) & UAS Bangalore
applicability_notes: Can be stored for over 2 years under dry traditional conditions without significant nutritional loss.

variety: Rabi Onion (N-53, Agrifound Light Red, Bhima Kiran)
crop_form: Cured Whole Bulbs with Dry Neck
moisture_basis: Outer Dry Scale Neck Moisture Max %
traditional_storage_methods: Traditional two-tier or three-tier bottom-ventilated bamboo structures (Kanda Chawl) with asbestos or thatched grass roof
Spreading bulbs on raised slatted wooden or bamboo platforms (50-60 cm above ground) to ensure continuous airflow from below
Thorough field-curing followed by shade-curing for 10-15 days until neck is tight and outer 2-3 scales are papery dry
Sorting and discarding all thick-neck ('bolters'), twin, or damaged bulbs before loading
ventilation_guidance: Continuous bottom-to-top natural draft ventilation is MANDATORY. High relative humidity (> 75%) causes rapid root emergence and black mould. Low humidity (< 60%) causes severe desiccation weight loss.
pest_prevention_guidance: Protect from Onion Thrips and Black Mould (Aspergillus niger). Clean structure walls and spray neem-based repellent on structure perimeter before storage.
spoilage_warning_signs: Softening or depression around the neck ('Neck Rot')
Black powdery spores under the outer dry papery scales (Aspergillus niger)
Green shoot tips emerging from the center (Sprouting)
White root button emergence at base plate due to excessive humidity (>75% RH)
Strong pungent ammoniacal decay odor
recommended_actions: Never store Kharif onions for long duration; only Rabi harvest with thin tight necks can be stored
If humidity rises above 75%, run exhaust fans or increase bottom airflow to strip moisture
Remove decaying or soft bulbs immediately to prevent contact rotting of adjacent healthy bulbs
source_name: ICAR - Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research (DOGR), Rajgurunagar & NHB Guidelines
applicability_notes: Applies strictly to well-cured Rabi season crop. In cold storage, conditions are 0-2°C with 65-70% RH; intermediate temperatures (12-18°C) cause disastrous sprouting.

variety: Kufri Jyoti, Kufri Pukhraj, Kufri Bahar, Kufri Chipsona
region: UP, West Bengal, Bihar, Punjab, Gujarat
traditional_storage_methods: Traditional heap/pit storage in cool shaded areas covered with thick dry straw (Kuttal/Khad system)
Pre-storage curing at 15-20°C and 90% RH for 10-14 days to promote suberization (wound healing of skin)
Complete darkness to prevent chlorophyll and toxic glycoalkaloid (solanine) synthesis
Sprinkling with dry sand layers in short-term village storage
ventilation_guidance: Cold stores require periodic fresh air flushing to keep CO2 levels below 2000-2500 ppm; CO2 accumulation causes internal black heart necrosis.
pest_prevention_guidance: Primary risks: Potato Tuber Moth (Phthorimaea operculella), Soft rot (Pectobacterium), Dry rot (Fusarium). Cover heaps with 5 cm layer of dry Lantana or Eucalyptus leaves to deter tuber moth.
spoilage_warning_signs: Skin turning green on light exposure (Solanine build-up)
Soft watery lesions leaking fluid with foul odor (Bacterial Soft Rot)
Dry sunken shriveled dark spots (Fusarium Dry Rot)
Internal black or brown discoloration ('Black Heart') due to poor aeration
Sprout growth longer than 1 cm
recommended_actions: Ensure curing period (suberization) is completed prior to lowering temperatures
Never expose potatoes to light during storage
Maintain relative humidity above 88% to avoid tuber shriveling, but prevent water droplets dripping from ceiling onto tubers
source_name: ICAR - Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI), Shimla
applicability_notes: Ware/table potatoes stored at 8-10°C prevent cold-induced sweetening. Seed potatoes are kept colder at 2-4°C.

region: Andhra Pradesh, MP, Karnataka, Odisha, Maharashtra
storage_type: Zero Energy Cool Chamber (ZECC) / Cold Room
traditional_storage_methods: Zero Energy Cool Chamber (ZECC) based on evaporative cooling with double-brick walls filled with wet river sand (lowers temp by 8-10°C and maintains RH > 85%)
Storing mature green fruit on raised slatted wooden crates lined with dry newspaper sheets
Stem-end down orientation to reduce moisture loss and mechanical pressure
ventilation_guidance: Moderate continuous ventilation required to dissipate accumulated ethylene gas which accelerates premature ripening and senescence.
pest_prevention_guidance: Protect from fruit flies, Alternaria rot, and Rhizopus soft rot. Handle gently during harvest to avoid skin punctures or bruising.
spoilage_warning_signs: Surface pitting, uneven color development, and failure to ripen when brought to room temp (Chilling Injury caused by temperatures < 10°C)
Water-soaked circular soft spots with grey-black mold (Alternaria Rot)
Wrinkling and loss of skin turgidity
recommended_actions: NEVER store mature green tomatoes below 10°C as irreversible chilling injury occurs
Keep turning/breaker tomatoes segregated from fully ripe red tomatoes
Replenish sand moisture daily if using Zero Energy Cool Chambers
source_name: ICAR - Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru & National Horticulture Board
applicability_notes: Harvest at breaker or turning stage for storage; fully red ripe tomatoes have only 4-7 days shelf life.

crop_form: Mature Hard Green Fruit with Intact Pedicel
traditional_storage_methods: Harvesting early morning with 8-10 mm pedicel intact to prevent latex sap burn on fruit skin
Traditional ripening / short storage in wooden boxes padded with dry paddy straw or wheat straw
Hot water treatment (52°C for 5 minutes) to eradicate latent Anthracnose and stem-end rot fungal spores
Desapping on specialized wash tables
ventilation_guidance: Cold stores require adequate air circulation (0.1 to 0.2 m/s) with ethylene scrubbing. Ethylene build-up triggers rapid softening.
pest_prevention_guidance: Guarding against Fruit Fly (Bactrocera dorsalis) and Anthracnose (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides). Use corrugated fiberboard (CFB) boxes with individual fruit paper wraps.
spoilage_warning_signs: Skin browning, dark scalding pits, and uneven blotchy ripening (Chilling Injury from temperatures < 11°C)
Dark tear-stain lesions or black sunken spots with pink spore masses (Anthracnose)
Softening at the stem end with sour vinous odor (Stem End Rot)
recommended_actions: Never set cold storage below 11.5°C for green mature mangoes
Dip fruits in warm water (52°C for 5 minutes) before packaging to control anthracnose
Ventilate storage room periodically to purge ethylene
source_name: ICAR - Central Institute for Subtropical Horticulture (CISH), Lucknow & APEDA Guidelines
applicability_notes: Chilling injury is catastrophic below 10°C. Ripening temperature is 20-22°C with 85% RH.

traditional_storage_methods: Harvesting bunches at 75-80% maturity; washing hands in alum water (1%) to coagulate latex
Packing in polythene bags (poly-bags with micro-perforations) inside CFB cartons
Traditional short storage in cool damp earthen cellars hanging bunches by nylon cords
ventilation_guidance: Continuous gentle air circulation with complete ethylene scrubbers. Even 0.1 ppm ethylene triggers irreversible ripening.
pest_prevention_guidance: Crown rot complex (Fusarium, Colletotrichum). Cut hands cleanly with curved dehanding knife and disinfect crown cut with alum paste.
spoilage_warning_signs: Dull smoky or grayish peel discoloration that fails to turn bright yellow upon ripening (Chilling Injury from temp < 12°C)
Blackening and fungal decay of the crown cut (Crown Rot)
Premature finger drop from the crown
recommended_actions: Strictly enforce minimum 13.0°C temperature floor; never store in standard household fridges
Ensure Relative Humidity stays above 90% to prevent finger neck shrinkage and dehydration
Isolate yellow ripening fruits immediately from green storage batches
source_name: ICAR - National Research Centre for Banana (NRCB), Tiruchirappalli
applicability_notes: Extremely susceptible to chilling injury. Cold storage must never dip below 12.5°C.
